newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise before Sunday elections.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise before Sunday elections.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.90 percent on Friday, pushed up by Thursday's news that bank SKB was seeking listing on foreign stock exchanges.
But the general feeling remained uneasy ahead of Slovenia's second general election on Sunday.
"If the Liberal Democrats remain in power, shares will rise significantly next week," Toni Apollonio, an analyst of A bank told Reuters.
"If the 'Spring' parties win, shares will stagnate, while traders wait for possible changes in government policy," he said.
Rightist parties have set up an informal alliance, called the "Slovenian Spring", comprising the People's Party, Christian Democrats and centre-right Social Democrats.
The SBI index rose 23.18 points to 1,223.88 to end the week 2.65 percent higher.

Overall 10 shares rose and seven fell, while seven were untraded. Total turnover fell to 392.7 million tolars after being exceptionally high on Thursday with 793.4 million on news of SKB's plans of a listing abroad.
"Most investors expect SKB shares to rise significantly after being listed abroad," Apollonio added.
Bank SKB had the highest turnover, closing 3.4 percent higher at 45,110 tolars on volume of 5,297 shares for a total turnover of 238 million tolars.
Health resort Terme Catez was the top gainer, rising 10 percent to 12,100 tolars on volume of 2,395 shares for total turnover of 28.9 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, falling 3.9 percent to close at 7,300 tolars on volume of 876 shares for total turnover of 6.2 million tolars.
